newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended the last full trading day of 1996 in a buoyant mood as the industrial index surged ahead, dealers said on Monday.
Following on from the new record set by Wall Street's industrial index on Friday London shares also hit a new peak and provided powerful impetus for the South African market.
The result was a healthy day's trading of about 350 million rand worth of shares that caught many traders by surprise in the middle of the usually listless holiday season.
"It was a hell of a lot better than we expected," one dealer said.
The all-share index rose 46.1 points to end at 6,629.2 as industrials edged up 73.8 points to finish the day at 7,889.4.

Dealers said that another factor weighing on the market's mind was the approaching year-end date for local unit trusts and so some of the upward momentum was coming from investors seeking to boost their books before the close-out.
"There was definitely some window dressing going on," one dealer said.
Anglos attracted heavy market interest, but ended unchanged at 255.50 rand while SA Breweries continued its recent strong recovery by putting on another 400 cents to end at 119.00 rand.
Other blue-chip gainers were Minorco which finished at 98.00 rand, up 125 cents, and Johnnic, which put on 50 cents to 51.25 rand.
Dealers said the outlook on Tuesday was for a listless day as the market will close at noon (1000 GMT) for the New Year's Eve holiday on Wednesday.
They added the market would also be especialy prone to window dressing. "You could see some very funny prices tomorrow," one said.
Gold shares had a good day as the bullion price ticked up and some analysts predicted it could soon launch an attack on the psychologically important $370 an ounce level.
The gold index put on 7.2 points to 1,502.5.
The futures market had a quiet but firm day as there was little futures-related buying in the spot market.
The all-share March contract edged up to 6,225/230 from 6,148 as the industrials contract rallied to 7,735/7745 from 7,643. Golds attracted little real interest but stood at 1,053/70 from 1,055.
